full_judgment:
6. Dr. Naim Ahmed, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the High Court Division erred in law in not considering that the writ petitioner never got any right, title and interest in the case property on the basis of the so-called sale deed No. 3704 dated 02.03.1971. He next submits that the High Court Division did not take into consideration the fact that the case property being included in the "Ka" list of the abandoned properties the present petitioner filed Case no. 329 of 1992 before the Court of Settlement, Dhaka, wherein the court directed the Government to delist the same and restore her in possession of the same, which was affirmed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 894 of 2002 as well as by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal. No. 352 of 2008.Thus pursuant to the aforesaid orders writ respondent No.4 issued the impugned letter which is lawful and the writ petitioner is bound to comply with the same. He further submits that after unsuccessfully moving upto this Division against the order of the Court of Settlement when the Government asked the writ petitioner (respondent No. 1) to vacate the case property, the writ petitioner, during the pendency of the Rule Nisi, also instituted Title Suit No. 42 of 2016 before the First Court of Joint District Judge, Thakurgaon for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land which is still pending in the trial court. Thus, Dr. Ahmed submits that since the title of the property in question has been raised in the suit by present respondent No.1 himself, the same cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction as this jurisdiction cannot be invoked to decide any disputed question of fact as the same can only be decided by a competent civil court on taking evidence. Hence, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division calls for interference of this Division. 

 9. From the materials on record it appears that, after the property in question was directed to be released from the list of abandoned properties and to hand over the same in favour of the present petitioner and all the attempts of the Government to set aside the said order failed the Executive Magistrate, (respondent No.4), sent the impugned letter directing the writ petitioner to vacate the case property and handover the same in favour of present petitioner which has been challenged in the present writ petition claiming that he purchased the said property by deed No. 3704 dated 02.03.1971. At the same time, he also filed Title Suit No. 42 of 2016 before the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Thakurgaon for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the same. The present petitioner does not admit the purchase deed No. 3704 of 02.03.1971 of the writ petitioner-respondent No.1 by dint of which he is claiming to be the owner of the said land to be genuine. Such denial of the heir of the transferee appears to have cast cloud on the title of the present respondent No. l. Side by side the claim of the present respondent No.1 on the basis of such deed also disputes the title of the present petitioner. Thus when the authenticity of that deed is raised the same is required to be decided by taking evidence for which civil Court is the appropriate forum which is competent to decide the same upon taking proper evidence. But the High Court Division without taking this aspect into consideration took the view that as the writ petitioner purchased the case property from the mother of writ respondent No.7, which made him the owner of the said property the Rule Nisi is required to be made absolute'. Such finding is not sustainable in the eye of law unless the genuineness of the document is proved by competent Court upon taking evidence.
